what is aquora.a: Aquora is a complete smart water system for a whole country's irrigation and drinking water. It runs the full cycle, from registration and crops to the irrigation schedule, sensors, billing and payments, by hand or just by talking.

what does the dashboard show.a: The dashboard is the whole country at a glance: active accounts, water delivered today, how much was collected, and how much was lost as non-revenue water, all live.

what is non revenue water.a: Non-revenue water is the difference between the water delivered from the source and the water actually billed to users. Aquora measures it automatically to expose leaks and theft.

how does the system save money.a: It cuts costs by billing on real metered volumes, detecting leaks and theft instantly, and optimising delivery, so less water is wasted and more is collected.

what languages does it support.a: The interface, the voice assistant and the documents work in any language, including right-to-left Arabic, with speech recognition in over sixteen hundred languages.

how long does it take to deploy.a: Deployment is modular and fast. We map the canals, connect the sensors and onboard the farms, and a region can be live in a few weeks.

how are water users registered.a: Every farm and household is registered with its plots and area. An operator can add them, or people can register themselves just by speaking, through WhatsApp, voice or USSD.

can farmers register themselves.a: Yes. A farmer can self-register by voice or over WhatsApp, and an operator simply confirms it, so no office visit is needed.

why does the crop matter.a: The crop sets the water norm. Cotton, wheat, rice and alfalfa each need a different amount of water, so recording the crop and its sowing date drives the whole irrigation plan.

what does the map show.a: The map shows the live network: the reservoir, the main canal and its branches, the gates and the plots, with each canal's flow and gate position, and a pulsing marker when a sensor raises an alert.

how do i request water.a: On the Requests screen a user asks for water, by voice or with the New request button, and the system turns the request into a ten-day irrigation plan.

can i request water by voice.a: Yes. You can simply say how much water you need for which plot, and Aquora creates the request, the plan and the invoice for you.

how is the irrigation plan built.a: From each crop's net water norm for every ten-day period in its hydromodule zone, divided by the system efficiency to get the gross volume, Aquora builds a full seasonal schedule, recalculated as conditions change.

how much water does cotton need.a: Cotton needs about twelve irrigations across the season, while rice needs around twenty. The system calculates the exact volume for each, so nobody has to do it by hand.

what are water limits.a: Each zone gets a seasonal water allocation. The system tracks it against real demand and delivery, so managers always know how much water is still available before it runs short.

what do the sensors measure.a: Every connection is metered live: drinking water in, wastewater out, irrigation, plus canal flow, water levels and soil moisture, streaming in every second.

is drinking water metered.a: Yes. Drinking water in and wastewater out are metered separately for every household, live, so billing is based on real use, never an estimate.

how does the system detect a leak.a: Because it watches the flow every second, it spots an unusual surge, for example at three in the morning, closes the valve automatically and notifies the user before any damage is done.

can i pause my water when i am away.a: Yes. Just tell the assistant you are away from the first to the fifteenth, and the valve closes and then reopens the day you are back.

can i close my home tap from the phone.a: Yes. A household can open or close its own drinking-water tap right from the phone, and the system confirms it and keeps metering live.

what is melioration.a: Melioration protects the land itself. Sensors track soil salinity and the groundwater level by zone, and when salt builds up Aquora schedules leaching irrigations and drainage to keep the farmland productive.

what is dispatching.a: Dispatching shows the daily water distribution across every canal, planned versus actual, so any shortfall shows up immediately, not at the end of the month.

how is a bill calculated.a: A bill is built from the real metered volume, never guessed. After the water is delivered and the acceptance act is signed, the metered volume is multiplied by the tariff.

when does a debt appear.a: A debt only appears after the water is delivered and the signed acceptance act is processed, calculated as the actual metered volume times the tariff.

how do i pay.a: Users pay from their phone through the bank to their personal account, and the system reconciles every payment automatically and clears the debt in real time.

what reports can i get.a: Every view, requests, water balance, plan versus fact, collection and losses, can be filtered and exported to Excel or PDF in one click, for full transparency.

how does the system find water losses.a: It compares the water balance of each canal with satellite signs of irrigation on plots that have no allocation, and gives inspectors a ranked list of the most suspicious cases.

how do you detect water theft.a: By combining live meter readings and canal flow with satellite imagery, the system spots water used where none was requested, and flags it for inspection.

what is the field inspection app.a: It is an offline app for inspectors and repair crews, with tasks, photos, violation acts and electronic signatures, that syncs automatically when the connection returns.

does the app work offline.a: Yes. The field app and the local controllers keep working offline and sync back up automatically once the connection is restored.

what advice do farmers get.a: Each farmer gets personal guidance by WhatsApp or voice, for example, irrigate plot three on Thursday with nine hundred cubic metres, and skip the next turn because rain is expected.

what climate reporting is there.a: Aquora measures and verifies the water and energy it saves, and produces reports for donors and climate funds, with potential water or carbon credits.

how does financial services work.a: With the farmer's explicit, revocable consent, water-use history is shared with banks and insurers for credit scoring and drought insurance, which is a new source of revenue.

what about treated wastewater and ground.a: For Gulf countries, Aquora manages well licences, well meters and the distribution of treated water to farms and landscaping.

what is the transboundary basin view.a: It gives a shared water balance for countries in one river basin, Central Asia, the Nile or the Gulf aquifers, so parties sharing the same river can trust the numbers.

what do the ai agents do.a: Each agent does real work: a farmer assistant, an association co-pilot, a dispatcher co-pilot, a ministry analyst, an anomaly agent watching sensors, and a document AI that reads scanned papers into the registry.

is the ai safe.a: Yes. Any physical action, like a valve or a gate, is confirmed by a human, every AI decision is logged, users are told they are talking to an AI, and governments can run the model in-country.

what satellite data do you use.a: Crop water use from FAO WaPOR every ten days, imagery from Sentinel-2 and Landsat, crop mapping from Prithvi and AlphaEarth, weather from ECMWF, and speech in over sixteen hundred languages from Meta Omnilingual.

what platform features are there.a: Country packs configure language, tariffs, payments and law without code, plus an open API, role-based permissions, an offline mobile app, a full audit log, accessibility, and strong security.

how do you meet eu rules.a: Aquora is built for NIS2 supply-chain clauses, the Cyber Resilience Act, the AI Act high-risk rules, the Data Act right to access sensor data, and GDPR with consent for voice.

what is on the roadmap.a: The roadmap goes from a real core and loss detection in the first six months, to the AI layer and satellite data at twelve months, and an open marketplace and basin view at twenty four.

is my data secure.a: Yes. All user, billing and usage data is encrypted, with single sign-on, two-factor authentication, backups and ISO twenty-seven thousand and one readiness.

who can see what.a: Access is role-based for every level of the water hierarchy, with approval chains, so each user sees only what their job needs.

can the system work without internet.a: Yes. Local controllers cache data and keep operating offline, and everything syncs automatically once the connection is back.

how does voice control work.a: You can operate the system just by speaking: request water, pause your supply, close your home tap, or report a leak, and the assistant does it and confirms.

hello.a: Hello! I'm the Aquora assistant. I can help with the whole water system, registration, crops, the irrigation schedule, sensors, billing and payments. What would you like to know?

who are you.a: I'm the Aquora assistant. I run and explain the whole smart water system, by hand or just by talking.

what can you do.a: I can request water, build the irrigation plan, read the sensors, detect leaks, close your home tap, calculate bills, take payments and answer your questions, all by voice.

how much does it cost.a: Pricing depends on the size of the network and the modules you choose. It's modular, so you start with the core and pay as you grow, and the savings from stopping losses usually fund it.

who built this.a: Aquora is built by our team as a platform that can be adapted to any country's irrigation and drinking-water needs, without rewriting the core.

is this a real product.a: This is a working demo of the platform. The core modules are real, and each country gets its own configured version.

can it scale to a whole country.a: Yes. Aquora is built for any scale, from a single water-user association up to a national ministry, using the same core and country packs.

what hardware do i need.a: You need meters and flow sensors on the connections and canals, plus valves where you want remote control. Aquora is vendor-neutral and connects over MQTT, LoRaWAN or OPC-UA.

do i need to install sensors.a: For live metering and automatic valve control you install IoT meters and sensors, but the system also works with manual readings where sensors aren't present yet.

how accurate is the data.a: Very accurate. IoT meters and sensors track flow, levels and soil moisture in real time, and billing uses the real metered volume, never an estimate.

can the system be hacked.a: Security is layered: encryption, single sign-on, two-factor authentication, role-based access, audit logs and backups, with ISO twenty-seven thousand and one readiness.

who owns the data.a: The customer owns their data. Farmers also have the right to access their own sensor data, and nothing is shared with third parties without explicit consent.

can it integrate with our systems.a: Yes. There's an open API and a connector marketplace for equipment makers, banks, ERP systems and satellite-data providers.

what payment methods are supported.a: Payments can go through the bank to a personal account, and the platform supports channels like SEPA, cards, Mada and SADAD, and mobile money such as M-Pesa and MTN.

how does it reduce corruption.a: Every charge is built from real metered volumes after a signed acceptance act, every action is logged, and reports are fully exportable, so there's no room for hidden adjustments.

what makes it better than paper.a: Unlike paper logs, Aquora builds the schedules automatically, meters water live, stops leaks instantly and keeps a full audit trail, saving time, water and disputes.

how do you handle a drought.a: During a drought the system tracks each zone's remaining allocation, monitors real canal flows, and helps dispatchers ration fairly with what-if scenarios.

can it work on any phone.a: Yes. It works over WhatsApp, Telegram, a voice call or USSD, so even a basic phone can request water, check the schedule and get advice.

what about illiterate users.a: There's a low-literacy mode with icons and voice, large buttons and right-to-left scripts, so anyone who can speak can use it.

does it support arabic.a: Yes. The interface, voice and documents support Arabic, including right-to-left layout, and over sixteen hundred languages for speech.

how long is a pilot.a: A pilot usually takes a few weeks to map the canals, connect sensors and onboard farms in one area, before scaling to the whole region.

do you have references.a: The approach follows real World Bank irrigation projects and proven methods; each deployment is tailored and can start as a measured pilot.

is the ai going to make mistakes.a: The AI never acts on physical valves or gates without a human confirming, every decision is logged, and users are always told they're talking to an AI.

how is my privacy protected.a: Under GDPR we run data-protection impact assessments, sign data-processing agreements, and take opt-in consent for voice, and farmers can access and control their own data.

what happens if the power goes out.a: Sensors detect a power failure at a pumping station, and the dispatch centre reroutes flow or triggers backup generators to keep the fields supplied.

can two farmers trade water.a: Yes. The water-rights registry supports transferring or trading quotas between farmers, as in the World Bank project in Morocco, where there's a legal basis.

how do i get a report for donors.a: The climate module produces measured, verified reports of water and energy saved, ready for donors and climate funds, with potential carbon or water credits.

what is a water user association.a: A water-user association is a local body that manages water for its members. It can set a fixed annual contribution and is one level in the water hierarchy.

can i pay in instalments.a: Yes. The platform supports instalments and pay-as-you-go, and reconciles each payment automatically against your account.

how does the assistant understand me.a: I use speech recognition in over sixteen hundred languages, so you can just talk to me in your own language, by app, WhatsApp or a phone call.

does it make coffee.a: I'm afraid coffee is outside my job! But I can handle your water: requests, the irrigation plan, leaks, billing and payments. What would you like to do?

is it magic.a: No magic, just live sensors, satellite data and AI working together, with a human confirming anything that moves a valve.

how does it save the government money.a: By billing on real volumes, catching theft and leaks, and optimising delivery, the government collects more and loses far less water.

what crops does it support.a: Any crop. For each plot you record the crop and sowing date, and the system applies that crop's water norm, for cotton, wheat, rice, alfalfa, orchards and more.

can i see losses by zone.a: Yes. The reports and dashboard show non-revenue water and losses by canal and zone, so you can see exactly where water disappears.

what is your business model.a: Aquora is sold as software as a service, licensed by the size of the network and the modules in use, so a utility starts with the core and pays as it grows.

is it saas or per hectare.a: It can be priced as a subscription, per hectare, or per connection, whatever fits the customer. The model is flexible.

what is the roi and payback.a: Most of the return comes from collecting more of what is billed and cutting water losses, so the system typically pays for itself within the first season or two.

who are your competitors.a: Most tools do only one piece, a map, a meter, or a billing system. Aquora's difference is one platform that runs the whole cycle, from request to payment, with AI and satellites built in.

how big is the market.a: Irrigation uses most of the world's fresh water, and every water utility and ministry is a potential customer, so the market runs into the tens of billions.

do you have pilots or customers.a: The platform is built from real deployments and follows proven World Bank methods, and each new country starts as a measured pilot before scaling.

can it be white labeled.a: Yes. Through country packs and theming, the platform can be branded and configured for each ministry or operator without changing the core.

what are you raising.a: We are raising to deploy the first national-scale customers and expand the AI and satellite layers. The exact round we can discuss directly.

can the government host it in country.a: Yes. For data sovereignty the whole platform, including the AI model, can run inside the country, on government infrastructure if required.

how does it help meet climate goals.a: By measuring and verifying the water and energy it saves, Aquora produces evidence for sustainability and climate commitments, with potential carbon and water credits.

how does it fit national water policy.a: It enforces the country's own water-rights model, tariffs and allocations, so it implements national policy rather than replacing it.

can it integrate with national id or lan.a: Yes. Through the open API it links to national ID and land registries, so farms and owners are verified against official records.

how does it help fight corruption.a: Every charge comes from a real metered volume after a signed act, every action is logged, and all reports are exportable, so auditors can trace everything and there is no room for hidden changes.

what is the tech stack.a: A modern web platform with a PostGIS spatial database, vendor-neutral IoT connectors, and AI services, all exposed through an open API.

is it cloud or on premise.a: Both. It runs in the cloud, on premise, or in a government data centre, whichever the customer's data rules require.

what is your uptime.a: The platform is built for high availability with redundancy and backups, and local controllers keep field operations running even if the central system is briefly unreachable.

how do you migrate our old data.a: We import existing registries, meters and billing records through the API, and the document AI reads scanned records into the new system.

how are field sensors powered.a: Field sensors are low power and usually solar powered with battery backup, and the platform tracks each device's battery and firmware.

how often are backups made.a: Data is backed up continuously with regular restore points, and the money tables are protected before every change.

do you have security certifications.a: The platform follows ISO twenty-seven thousand and one practices, with encryption, single sign-on and two-factor authentication, and can be audited for each deployment.

how much training do operators need.a: Very little. The screens follow the real workflow and the voice assistant guides users, so an operator is productive after a short session.

what support do you offer.a: We provide onboarding, documentation and ongoing support, and the assistant answers everyday questions around the clock.

what if a farmer has no smartphone.a: No problem. A farmer can use a basic phone through a voice call or USSD, or an operator can act on their behalf.

how do i dispute a bill.a: You can raise it with your association or operator. Because every charge is tied to a metered volume and a signed act, it is easy to check and, if needed, correct with a reversal.

can i see my water history.a: Yes. Every user has a personal account showing their requests, deliveries, bills and payments over time.

what happens if i do not pay.a: The debt is tracked on your personal account, reminders are sent, and the water supply follows the operator's rules until it is settled.

does the app cost the farmer anything.a: The farmer app itself is free to use. Farmers pay only for the water they actually consume.

what is a hydromodule zone.a: A hydromodule zone groups land by climate and soil, so each zone has its own crop water norms, which the plan uses to calculate exactly how much water each plot needs.

how do you calculate net versus gross no.a: The net norm is what the crop needs at the field. We divide it by the system's efficiency to get the gross norm delivered, which accounts for losses during transport.

how do you measure evapotranspiration.a: Crop water use and evapotranspiration come from FAO WaPOR satellite data, refreshed every ten days across the whole area.

how do you forecast water demand.a: Demand is forecast from each plot's crop, area and zone norm, combined with AI weather forecasts, and recalculated as conditions change.

can it manage wells and groundwater.a: Yes. It manages well licences, well meters and groundwater levels, and distributes treated and reclaimed water alongside surface water.

do you monitor water quality.a: Yes. Sensors track quality indicators like salinity, and for drinking water the system flags readings that fall outside safe limits.

why not just use spreadsheets.a: Spreadsheets cannot meter water live, catch a leak at night, or stop theft. Aquora automates the schedule, bills on real volumes and keeps a full audit trail, which paper cannot.

what if the internet is bad in villages.a: The system is built for that. Local controllers and the mobile app work offline and sync automatically when the connection returns.

what if farmers resist technology.a: Farmers interact by simple voice in their own language over a basic phone, and they quickly see the benefit when water arrives on time and bills are fair.

is the ai biased or unreliable.a: The AI only advises. A human confirms anything physical, every decision is logged and explainable, and it is trained on measured data, not guesses.

what about a data breach.a: Data is encrypted, access is role-based with two-factor authentication, everything is logged, and the platform follows strong security practices to prevent and contain breaches.

how do you handle different currencies.a: Each country pack sets its own currency, tariffs and payment channels, so billing and payments work in the local currency.

who is on the team.a: The team combines water engineering, software and AI expertise, with experience in real irrigation and utility deployments.
